source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Social/Political Life Ch. 4 (Grassroots Democracy – Part 3: Urban Areas).

sections.heading: 1. Urban Local Government
points: Towns and cities are governed by **urban local bodies** (municipal government).
They are the urban counterpart of the rural Panchayati Raj.
Given **constitutional status** by the **74th Constitutional Amendment (1992)**.

sections.heading: 2. Types of Urban Local Bodies
points: **Municipal Corporation** — for **large cities** (e.g. metros).
**Municipality / Municipal Council** — for **smaller towns**.
**Nagar Panchayat** — for **small / transitional towns** (areas becoming urban).
The type depends on the **size and population** of the town.

sections.heading: 3. Structure
points: The city is divided into **wards**; people elect a **Ward Councillor** from each ward.
**Mayor** = the elected **head** of a Municipal Corporation (largely a **ceremonial/leadership** role, presides over meetings).
**Municipal Commissioner** = an **appointed** official (usually IAS) who is the **administrative head** and runs day-to-day work.
**Ward committees** help manage local issues at the ward level.

sections.heading: 4. Functions
points: **Water supply**, **sanitation and garbage collection**, **drainage and sewage**.
**Street lighting**, **roads**, **parks**, **markets** and **public health**.
Registering **births and deaths**; running schools, hospitals and **fire services**.
Controlling **building/construction** and keeping the city clean and safe.

sections.heading: 5. Funds
points: Main income: **property tax**, **water tax**, and other local taxes and fees.
**Grants** from the State and Union governments.
Funds are used for city services and development.

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Urban local bodies: Municipal Corporation (big cities) → Municipality/Council (towns) → Nagar Panchayat (small/transitional towns).
74th Constitutional Amendment (1992) = constitutional status to urban local bodies.
Mayor = elected head (ceremonial); Municipal Commissioner = appointed administrative head.
City divided into wards → each elects a Ward Councillor.
Main income = property tax + water tax + grants.

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **74th** Amendment = urban bodies; **73rd** = rural (Panchayati Raj) — don't swap.
**Mayor** is elected (ceremonial head); **Municipal Commissioner** is appointed (real administrative head).
Order by town size: **Municipal Corporation > Municipality > Nagar Panchayat**.
Property tax is a key **own source** of income for city governments.
